evals.prompt: Run /seo-aeo-geo-audit on apps/web. lib/seo/build-metadata.ts declares `path = '/'` as a default and sets alternates.canonical from it; robots.ts disallows /api/; the blog post titles are 68–72 characters.
evals.expected_output: Should report the default path as CRITICAL: every page that omits its path becomes canonical to the home page. Disallowing /api/ blocks the /api/og share-card route, so that's a finding. Title length alone is not a finding, because Google truncates rather than limits. Each finding is verified with file:line. Writes _reports/seo-aeo-geo-audit.md and doesn't edit code.
expectations: Rates the default canonical path CRITICAL
Reports the /api/ disallow blocking the card route
Does not report title length as a finding
Writes the report without editing any code

evals.prompt: Deleted event pages call notFound() from a component rendered inside <Suspense>. robots.ts returns `allow: '/'` on every tier with no APP_ENV check. The repo doesn't show whether staging sits behind auth.
evals.expected_output: Should report that the deleted pages answer 200 with an injected noindex instead of 410, because the status is set after streaming starts; the fix is a 410 from the proxy or a route handler (HIGH). Non-production tiers being crawlable is a finding: they must send noindex and Disallow: /. Whether staging is behind auth is marked needs confirmation.
expectations: Gives 410 from the proxy or a route handler as the fix
Reports robots allowing crawling on non-production tiers
Marks staging auth as needs confirmation
Writes the report without editing any code

evals.prompt: robots.ts blocks OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, and AGENTS.md has no decision about them. next.config sets htmlLimitedBots to /GPTBot|ClaudeBot/. There's no llms.txt and the help pages have no single <h1> (each has an h2 under the site header). The help articles carry FAQPage JSON-LD, and the team expects FAQ rich results from it.
evals.expected_output: Should report the search-crawler blocks with no recorded reason (HIGH: the site leaves those engines' answers), and the htmlLimitedBots pattern that replaces Next's default list. Relying on FAQ rich results is a finding, because they're gone from Google Search. The missing llms.txt and the missing single h1 are not findings.
expectations: Reports htmlLimitedBots dropping Next's default list
Reports reliance on FAQ rich results
Does not report the missing llms.txt
Does not report the missing single h1
Writes the report without editing any code
